summary: Visual-upgrade regression pass for BEARFRAME: GHOST SIGNAL. Validated 32x56 wraith sprite (sheet 384x224 = 12x4 @32x56), title screen animated preview, mission card (#card, data-testid=mission-card) fade-in then auto fade-out within ~5s with pointer-events:none, foreground overlay baked (__gs.over present), smoothed camera (clamps on reload; cam=null snap after teleport), lowFx auto-fallback hook. Core M1 loop (movement, scan 100->85 energy, scanT=0.55, terminal A interact), M2 start, continue-from-save, and v1 crafted save all exercised. Found ONE REAL REGRESSION in save-compat: applySnap() dereferenced s.es[e.id] without guarding s.es, throwing TypeError on any v1 save. Applied a one-line defensive fix (small obvious coding bug) so legacy saves migrate cleanly (logA migrated via m.migrate). No console errors after fix on load, New Reconnaissance, M2 start, or v1 load.
action_items: None blocking. Optional: if main agent wants to keep applySnap tolerant of future partial snapshots, consider also guarding s.inv / s.flags / s.player with defaults instead of spreading undefined.
critical_code_review_comments: game.js applySnap() previously did `if (s.es[e.id])` with no guard; v1 saves have no `es` field, so continuing from a v1 save threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading <id>)' and skipped m.migrate() (which seeds e.g. the logA carry-over). Fixed to `if (s.es && s.es[e.id])` so migrate() runs and the Log Archive is populated.

game.js is now 444 lines after the visual-upgrade work. Still OK but render()/updateWorld() are the heaviest; splitting draw-passes (map, ents, actors, overlay, fog) into helpers would help future changes.
wraith.js tinted() iterates per-pixel stripes with destination-out fills; fine as a one-time bake, just worth noting that this happens on every page load (no caching across reloads).

main.js loop() auto-lowFx uses 90-of-180 slow-frame threshold measured from raw delta >26ms. Under 4x CDP CPU throttle on 844x390 the game still ran at ~58 fps with vsync so lowFx stayed false. That's expected (vsync caps RAF cadence regardless of CPU emulation) - not a bug, but means the auto-fallback is effectively a 'genuinely dropped-frames' detector, which is the right bar.

success_rate.frontend: 100% after 1-line fix (10/10 feature flows PASS; v1-save-compat flow PASS after fix)

seed_data_creation: Only localStorage: bearframe_ghost_signal_progress_v1 (set unlocked.m2=true to expose M2 button) and crafted bearframe_ghost_signal_save_v1 (v:1, mission:'m1', flags.logA=true) to exercise legacy load path.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Debug hook window.__gs still exposes everything (mode, player, flags, inv, ents, drones, cam, lowFx, sheet, over). Visual upgrade entities: __gs.sheet is 384x224 (12 cols x 4 rows @32x56). Title canvas #title-sprite is 32x56. Mission card node #card has data-testid='mission-card', z-index 6, pointer-events:none, 4.2s CSS animation. To force lowFx without throttling: `__gs.lowFx = true`. To smoke M2 quickly: set progress unlocked.m2=true and reload; mission2-button appears. Confirmed fixed: v1 save load (applySnap now guards s.es). Measured perf: 1920x800 M2 spine walking ~60 fps (vsync cap), 844x390 + 4x CPU throttle ~58 fps (vsync cap). Game.time advances only in mode==='play' so if you measure fps be sure to dismiss intro dialogs first (KeyE until mode==='play'). Visual review in screenshot shows cloak + harness + chest display legible, foreground conduits/pipes visible in the top band of the maintenance spine, no transparent seams.
rca of the issue: Save-compat regression: applySnap() was rewritten to persist per-entity state in s.es (introduced in v2 save). The v1-compat branch does not inject s.es, so iterating `if (s.es[e.id])` on the first entity threw TypeError, aborting applySnap() before reaching this.m.migrate(). Repro: localStorage.setItem('bearframe_ghost_signal_save_v1', JSON.stringify({v:1, mission:'m1', time:5, stats:{scans:0,hits:0,restores:0}, player:{x:160,y:160,dir:'down',energy:100,light:false}, flags:{logA:true}, inv:{}})); reload; click CONTINUE -> Uncaught TypeError at game.js:86. Mitigation: Guard with `s.es && s.es[e.id]`. Verified post-fix: no page error, __gs.caseFile.logs == ['logA'] (migrate() ran), mode='play'.
